problem: The statement 'Equality, Parseval's identity, holds only for a full orthonormal basis' is false. For a partial orthonormal set, equality in Bessel can hold for a particular vector u whenever u lies in the span of that set, for example u = 0. The correct restriction is that Parseval's identity holds for every u only when the orthonormal set is a full basis.
fix: Bessel is an inequality for an orthonormal set. Equality for a particular u holds exactly when u lies in the span of the set; for a full orthonormal basis, Parseval's identity gives equality for every u.

problem: The text calls the partial orthonormal set 'the basis' even though it has just said the set is not necessarily a full basis. This is imprecise and can confuse students about what is being projected onto.
fix: The sum is the squared norm of the orthogonal projection of u onto span{e₁,…,e_m}.

problem: 'Gram–Schmidt turns the added vectors into a basis of W⊥' is ambiguous. If Gram–Schmidt is applied only to the added vectors, they need not become orthogonal to W. The process must be applied to the whole extended basis, starting with the basis of W.
fix: Apply Gram–Schmidt to the whole extended basis, starting with the basis of W; the added vectors then become a basis of W⊥.
